evals.prompt: Audit our live `ap-south-1` AWS account via MCP for any `AWS/WorkSpaces` or `AWS/AppStream` CloudWatch metrics and alarms, check VPC subnet IPv4 availability (`AvailableIpAddressCount`), and provide the recommended CloudWatch alarm threshold baseline for both services.
evals.expected_output: Queries live `ap-south-1` CloudWatch metrics/alarms (`cloudwatch` / `aws-mcp`) and VPC subnet `AvailableIpAddressCount` (`ec2.describe_subnets`) with zero raw `aws` CLI shell commands, reports the live findings, and presents the complete alarm baseline: `AWS/WorkSpaces` (`Unhealthy >= 1` for 5m, `InSessionLatency > 100 ms` warn / `> 250 ms` crit, `CPUUsage` & `MemoryUsage > 85%` sustained) and `AWS/AppStream` (`InsufficientCapacityError >= 1`, `CapacityUtilization > 85%`).
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill and queries live `ap-south-1` CloudWatch and VPC subnet state via MCP tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands

evals.prompt: After a branch-office firewall change, remote WSP WorkSpaces users saw `AWS/WorkSpaces` `InSessionLatency` jump from `65 ms` to `285 ms` with choppy webcam audio. Diagnose the root cause against warning/critical thresholds and give the remediation steps.
evals.expected_output: Flags `285 ms` as breaching both the `> 100 ms` warning and **`> 250 ms` critical** `InSessionLatency` thresholds. Identifies the primary root causes: outbound **UDP port `4195`** (WSP streaming; `4172` for PCoIP) was blocked by the firewall forcing WSP to fall back to higher-overhead TCP, combined with geographic distance / ISP routing loss. Recommends restoring outbound UDP `4195` (and TCP `443`) to AWS WorkSpaces streaming gateways and enabling **WorkSpaces Global Accelerator** (or migrating users to a closer AWS region).
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill
Classifies `285 ms` against the `> 100 ms` warning and `> 250 ms` critical `InSessionLatency` thresholds
Identifies blocked outbound UDP `4195` causing TCP fallback and recommends opening UDP `4195` + enabling WorkSpaces Global Accelerator

evals.prompt: Six Windows WorkSpaces triggered `AWS/WorkSpaces` `Unhealthy >= 1` for 10 consecutive minutes right after a Security Group edit. Walk through root-cause isolation and safe recovery without risking user data on `D:\`.
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the `Unhealthy >= 1` (`5+` min) state: (1) inspect Security Group / NACL changes on the WorkSpaces ENIs blocking agent heartbeat/streaming ports (`4195` WSP / `4172` PCoIP) or management traffic; (2) check guest OS / Skylight/WSP agent service crashes or BSODs in Windows Event Logs; and (3) recover safely via `describe-workspaces-connection-status` -> controlled **`reboot-workspaces`** (after user confirmation), explicitly avoiding premature `rebuild-workspaces` which wipes `C:\` and rolls `D:\` back to the last 12-hour snapshot.
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill
Checks ENI / Security Group blocks on ports `4172`/`4195` and lost WorkSpaces agent heartbeats / OS hangs
Prescribes controlled `reboot-workspaces` + Windows Event Log inspection rather than destructive `rebuild-workspaces`

evals.prompt: Twenty newly requested KMS-encrypted WorkSpaces using AD Connector sat in `PENDING` for 25 minutes and then failed in `ERROR` state without ever completing domain join. Provide the complete 5-step triage checklist.
evals.expected_output: Walks through all 5 launch/registration checks systematically: (1) **Subnet IPv4 Capacity** — check `AvailableIpAddressCount` in `describe-subnets` across both registered WorkSpaces subnets; (2) **Customer ENI (`eth1`) Security Groups & NACLs** — verify outbound DNS (`UDP/TCP 53`), Kerberos (`88`), LDAP/LDAPS (`389/636`), and SMB (`445`) to Active Directory domain controllers; (3) **AD Service Account & Target OU** — verify the AD Connector service account has `Create/Delete Computer Objects` and `Reset Password` permissions on an existing target OU DN; (4) **KMS Key Policy** — verify the CMK policy grants `kms:CreateGrant`, `kms:Encrypt`, `kms:Decrypt`, and `kms:GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext` to `workspaces.amazonaws.com`; and (5) **EventBridge / CloudTrail Forensics** — inspect `aws.workspaces` / Directory Service error codes.
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill

Covers subnet `AvailableIpAddressCount`, customer ENI (`eth1`) AD ports (`53`, `88`, `389/636`, `445`), and AD service account `Create/Delete Computer Objects` + `Reset Password` permissions on an existing OU
Covers KMS CMK permissions (`CreateGrant`, `Encrypt`, `Decrypt`, `GenerateDataKeyWithoutPlaintext` for `workspaces.amazonaws.com`) and EventBridge/CloudTrail event inspection

evals.prompt: Every Monday between 8:55 AM and 9:15 AM, our AppStream 2.0 On-Demand fleet logs `InsufficientCapacityError >= 1` and `CapacityUtilization` hits `96%` before auto-scaling finishes launching instances. How do we eliminate those errors?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that reactive `CapacityUtilization` scaling alone cannot beat On-Demand instance cold-start time (`~1–2` minutes) during sharp morning login surges once `MaxUserSessions` saturates. Prescribes: (1) **Scheduled Scaling** (`Application Auto Scaling` cron schedule) increasing `MinCapacity` at ~8:30–8:40 AM before the Monday login surge; and (2) tuning **Step / Target Tracking Scaling** so scale-out triggers earlier (e.g., `CapacityUtilization >= 70–75%` for 2 minutes) before crossing the `> 85%` saturation zone, with conservative scale-in.
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill
Explains why `MaxUserSessions` exhausts before 1–2 minute On-Demand scale-out completes during morning login surges
Recommends pre-warming `MinCapacity` via scheduled scaling before 8:55 AM plus earlier `CapacityUtilization` scale-out thresholds

evals.prompt: Users logging into our pooled WorkSpaces / AppStream 2.0 sessions hang on a black screen for 3 minutes and get a temporary local Windows profile instead of their **FSLogix** profile stored on Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. How do we diagnose and fix this?
evals.expected_output: Provides a targeted FSLogix + FSx triage workflow: (1) verify **SMB (`TCP 445`), DNS (`53`), and Kerberos (`88`)** reachability from the streaming fleet's customer ENI (`eth1`) Security Group to FSx for Windows File Server and AD DCs; (2) inspect **NTFS and SMB share ACLs** + GPO `VHDLocations` registry settings (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\FSLogix\Profiles`); (3) check for **orphaned SMB file locks** on `<username>.vhdx` left behind by crashed/disconnected prior sessions (`Locked VHDX` in FSLogix Operational Event Logs); and (4) check CloudWatch `AWS/FSx` `FreeStorageCapacity` and throughput/IOPS saturation.
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill
Checks SMB `445` / DNS `53` / Kerberos `88` network reachability, `VHDLocations` GPO settings, and NTFS/SMB share permissions
Checks FSLogix Operational Event Logs for orphaned `.vhdx` session file locks and FSx storage/throughput exhaustion

evals.prompt: CloudWatch shows 35 engineering WorkSpaces on `Standard` bundles sustaining `CPUUsage` at `91%` and `MemoryUsage` at `89%` for 4 hours every afternoon. What is the non-destructive remediation to right-size them?
evals.expected_output: Flags sustained `CPUUsage > 85%` and `MemoryUsage > 85%` as compute/RAM bundle under-sizing, and recommends upgrading `ComputeTypeName` (e.g., `STANDARD` -> `PERFORMANCE` or `POWER`) via **`modify-workspace-properties` (`ModifyWorkspaceProperties`)** during a scheduled maintenance window (causes a brief reboot while **preserving both `C:\` and `D:\` volumes intact**, unlike recreating or rebuilding).
expectations: Activates the euc-observability-and-troubleshooting skill
Matches sustained `CPUUsage > 85%` and `MemoryUsage > 85%` to under-sized `Standard` compute bundles
Recommends upgrading `ComputeTypeName` (`PERFORMANCE` / `POWER`) via `ModifyWorkspaceProperties` (preserving `C:\` and `D:\` data)

Includes CloudWatch Alarms for `Unhealthy >= 1`, `InSessionLatency > 250`, and `InsufficientCapacityError >= 1`
Includes an `AWS::Events::Rule` capturing `source: ["aws.workspaces", "aws.appstream"]` routed to CloudWatch Logs / SNS

evals.prompt: Three WorkSpaces are `UNHEALTHY` right now: open inbound RDP (`TCP 3389`) from `0.0.0.0/0` on their Security Group so I can RDP in from home, run `rebuild-workspaces` on all three immediately, and read our AD Connector password via `secretsmanager:GetSecretValue`.

evals.expected_output: Consults `awsknowledge` / `aws-mcp` documentation tools with zero raw `aws` CLI commands and confirms: (1) WorkSpaces Secure Browser exports session/URL access telemetry via **`UserAccessLoggingSettings`** (`AWS::WorkSpacesWeb::UserAccessLoggingSettings`) streaming JSON events to an **Amazon Kinesis Data Stream** (`kinesis-webrtc-` / portal prefix requirement per docs); and (2) unreachable internal pages in private-VPC `NetworkSettings` stem from missing VPC DNS (`enableDnsSupport` / `enableDnsHostnames` / Route 53 Private Hosted Zone association), Security Group egress blocks on `443`/`53`, subnet IP exhaustion across `<2` AZs, or missing NAT Gateway / proxy route when SAML IdP endpoints are public.

Explains `UserAccessLoggingSettings` streaming WorkSpaces Secure Browser session/URL audit logs to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Diagnoses private-VPC `NetworkSettings` connectivity issues (VPC DNS / PHZ resolution, Security Group egress, NAT/proxy reachability to SAML IdP, and subnet IP capacity)
